correctness.rationale: Let y=ax+b and x=cy+d with independent uniform endpoint constraints. The map (a,b,c,d) to (a,c,X,Y) has Jacobian |1−ac| and the admissible intervals I(x,y),I(y,x) are derived by enforcing endpoint coordinates in [0,1]. Integrating 1−ac across two intervals and reducing by square dihedral symmetry yields f=u[4v(1−v)−u]/[4(1−u)²v²(1−v)²]. My independently written slope-interval/Jacobian implementation matched the closed formula for 1,200 random interior pairs; quadrature across the four fundamental wedges gave total probability 0.9999999999999997. The derivative in T=v(1−v) and diagonal u show unique peak f(center)=4. Corner rescaling integrates to 5/12 by dominated convergence; a vertical marginal has 2x log(1/x)+O(x), giving x² log(1/x)+O(x²). The proof distinguishes equal-edge endpoint sampling from motion-invariant lines and excludes boundary null sets.
